headline: FAA's nationwide ground stop halts US flights amid shifting cause reports
summary: The FAA ordered a nationwide ground stop on November 13, halting US flights for about five hours over what officials initially called a communications failure. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy later attributed it to obsolete equipment and routine copper-to-fiber maintenance work, while a later report said the FAA traced the cause to a malfunctioning feature in two newly installed network routers.

claims.statement: On November 13, the FAA ordered a nationwide ground stop halting flights across the US.

sources.quote: FAA Grounds All US Flights Until Further Notice
US government grounds all flights across the United States ‘due to extraordinary circumstances’

claims.statement: The ground stop was initially attributed to a communications failure affecting air traffic control systems.

sources.quote: The government cited a nationwide communications failure among air traffic control systems as the reason for the sudden grounding on Friday.
following communication issues impacting multiple Air Route Traffic Control Centers

claims.statement: The ground stop lasted about five hours and was lifted Friday evening.

sources.quote: The five-hour ordeal ended Friday evening.
FAA has lifted its third-ever nationwide ground stop

claims.statement: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy attributed the outage to obsolete, malfunctioning equipment.

sources.quote: Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy blamed obsolete equipment for the outage.
the transportation secretary blamed it on old and malfunctioning air traffic control system.

claims.statement: Duffy said the ground stop stemmed from work replacing old copper wire with fiber optic line, calling it routine maintenance rather than a major modernization effort.

claims.statement: A later report said the FAA determined the ground stop was caused by a malfunctioning feature in two newly installed network routers.
